Quick Start Scenario

The
Shepherd's
Transit

Mission Type

Route Security / VIP Escort

Environment

Semi-rural MSR, agricultural fields, low compounds

Timeframe

Early Morning → Midday (2010)

Tone

Pressure, ambiguity, consequence

Session Length

1 Sandbox Turn (single session)

Players

2–4 PCs + NPC patrol or Solo

Situation

A senior officer is scheduled to transit the AO under escort later today. The Main Supply Route (MSR) must be cleared of mines and potential ambush sites prior to his movement.

A patrol will deploy from Fort Qalat, insert a sniper overwatch team at Checkpoint 1 (CP1), proceed to Checkpoint 2 (CP2) to link up with Company A, receive the VIP, and return via CP1 to recover the snipers.

Recent enemy activity indicates heightened insurgent interest along the route.

Civilian traffic remains present and unpredictable.

Mission

1st Squad will:

  • Sweep the MSR for mines and ambush indicators

  • Insert a four-man sniper overwatch team at CP1

  • Link up with Company A at CP2

  • Escort the VIP safely back to Fort Qalat

  • Recover the sniper team during exfiltration

Mission Success: The VIP reaches Fort Qalat alive. Nothing else is guaranteed.

Execution

This mission is not scripted. Events will unfold based on:

  • Patrol movement

  • Timing

  • Player decisions

  • Enemy reactions

The Game Master should prepare events, not outcomes. Enemy forces operate independently and will exploit hesitation, predictability, and escalation. Quiet success is real success.

Enemy Forces

Local insurgent cells are active in the AO.

They:

  • Blend with civilian populations

  • Employ surface-laid IEDs

  • Use small arms and light machine guns

  • Operate with motorcycles and light vehicles

Enemy intent is observation and pressure, not decisive engagement.

Friendly Forces

  • 1st Squad (player-led patrol)

  • Attached sniper team

  • Company A (separate element, limited coordination)

Fire support and CASEVAC are available but delayed.

Civilians

Civilians are present along the MSR and in surrounding fields.

They may:

  • Require aid

  • Obstruct movement

  • Provide intelligence

  • Be exploited by enemy forces

Civilian interaction will affect Trust and long-term campaign outcomes.

Special Notes (Gm)

  • This scenario follows the events of Ambush at Dawn

  • Enemy forces may be acting in response to prior patrol actions

  • The patrol may be deliberately herded into follow-on engagements

  • Escalation solves today and complicates tomorrow

Track consequences. Let silence matter.

(Read To Players)

Your chief, Captain Mayers, enters the tent. He’s in mid 30-s, bald and shaved, with a scar from fire on his neck. With a low and commanding voice, he says…

“Tomorrow evening, the Colonel will transit through our AO. Company A will escort him to Checkpoint 2 along the MSR.”

“Your mission is to clear the MSR of mines, insert a sniper overwatch team, and link up with Company A to escort the Colonel back to the FOB.”

“You will depart at 0300 with four armored vehicles. Proceed to CP1, insert the sniper team, then continue to CP2.”

“Company A will arrive at CP2 by 1200 local.”

“Fire support is limited. CASEVAC is 30 minutes. No ISR. Clear weather.”

“Success equals escorting the VIP safely back to base.”

“Any questions?”

Pre-Mission Phase
(Player Agency)

Before departure, allow players to:

  • Assign vehicles and seating.

  • Choose gunner positions.

  • Decide sniper distribution.

  • Conduct PCCs / PCIs.

  • Rehearse contingencies.

Vehicle Layout:

Where players sit matters later. Who rides where determines exposure, casualties, and chaos.

Reward preparation with minor bonuses (reduced DRMs, initiative edge, extra intel).

VEHICLE 1

Command & Alpha Fire Team

VEHICLE COMMANDER SSgt Armando Suarez

DRIVER

Cpl Brad Ho (stays with vehicle)

GUNNER

Cpl Ethan Kline (stays with vehicle)

PASSENGERS

• Sgt Matt Blanco • PFC Brad Holstein

DISMOUNT TEAM

SSgt Suarez, Sgt Blanco, PFC Holstein

NOTES Command element. Driver and gunner provide vehicle security while others dismount.

Should an open seat be needed, the squad will leave PFC Holstein behind for the VIP, Colonel.

VEHICLE 2

Heavy Weapons Team

VEHICLE COMMANDER Sgt Terry Cooper

DRIVER

LCpl Fred Lipski (stays with vehicle)

GUNNER

PFC Todd Smalls (stays with vehicle)

PASSENGERS

• HM3 Al Grant (Doc)

• Sniper Team Member (blends in)

DISMOUNT TEAM

Sgt Cooper (with M240 option), Doc Grant

NOTES Heavy weapons capability. Corpsman available for casualties.

VEHICLE 3

Bravo Fire Team

VEHICLE COMMANDER Sgt Marcus Dempsey

DRIVER

PFC Derrick Hollis (stays with vehicle)

GUNNER

Spc Shawn Price ‘Not Right’ (stays with vehicle)

PASSENGERS

• Cpl Tony Whitfield

• Sniper Team Member (blends in)

DISMOUNT TEAM

Sgt Dempsey, Cpl Whitfield

NOTES Breacher capability with Sgt Dempsey.

VEHICLE 4

Charlie Fire Team

VEHICLE COMMANDER Sgt Aaron Whitaker

DRIVER

PFC Travis Monroe (stays with vehicle)

GUNNER

Cpl Brian Littleton (stays with vehicle)

PASSENGERS

• Spc Devon Johnson

• HM3 Al Grant (Doc)

DISMOUNT TEAM

Sgt Whitaker, Spc Johnson

NOTES Breacher capability with Sgt Whitaker.

Employment Doctrine

  • Security Protocol: Driver and gunner always stay with the vehicle for security

  • Sniper Integration: Three-man sniper team distributes across vehicles to blend in when dismounting

  • Flexibility: Three open seats available across Vehicles 2, 3, and 4 for mission-specific attachments

  • Fire Support: M240 GPMG can be dismounted with Sgt Cooper for heavy fire support
